## Change the service without losing the handover

When cleaning is not working, a fresh start can help. But a new contractor still needs a clear scope, practical access and a shared understanding of the condition on day one. Otherwise, the same uncertainty can move from one provider to the next.

This is a planning guide for offices considering a change in Newcastle CBD or Lake Macquarie. It is not a termination notice or legal advice. Check your existing agreement and obtain advice on unclear obligations before agreeing an end date or replacement commencement.

## First establish what is actually going wrong

Write down a few specific examples. Record the area, agreed task, expected frequency and when the issue was observed. Keep confidential documents, people and screens out of any photos.

Sort each issue into one of four groups:

| Issue | What to establish before changing providers |
| --- | --- |
| Included work missed | Is the task scheduled and accessible, and has it been raised through the agreed process? |
| Scope no longer fits | Has attendance, use, layout or the required task frequency changed? |
| Access or coordination failed | Were keys, inductions, service windows and restricted areas clear? |
| Maintenance or specialist need | Does the issue require repair or work outside the ordinary cleaning scope? |

This helps a new provider understand the job. It also gives your current provider a specific issue to address if you choose to discuss it. Avoid assuming a visible problem proves neglect or that a change will automatically solve it.

## Before you commit: align the dates and obligations

Review the current agreement's notice, renewal, payment, equipment and handover arrangements. Confirm the final service date and the incoming provider's readiness before relying on a changeover date. Do not assume there is a standard notice period that applies to every contract.

Tell building management about the planned change where appropriate. Confirm any induction, approved-access, lift, parking and waste-room requirements. A Newcastle CBD tenancy may share facilities with other occupiers; distinguish your responsibilities from the landlord's or building manager's arrangements.

The incoming provider should assess the site and supply a written proposal. Compare [cleaning costs against the whole scope](/blog/commercial-cleaning-cost-newcastle), including initial detail work, rather than accepting a matching headline price against different tasks.

## Build one handover register

The register should track responsibilities and status. It should not contain security credentials.

| Handover item | Record |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | Final version, included areas, task frequencies and exclusions |
| Contacts | Workplace contact, provider contact and building-management route |
| Dates | Final outgoing visit, agreed incoming start and first review |
| Keys and passes | Custodian, authorised transfer, return confirmation and outstanding items |
| Alarm procedure | Who arranges secure instructions and confirms authorisation |
| Equipment and stock | Ownership, removal or transfer, storage and replenishment responsibilities |
| Site instructions | Restricted areas, delicate surfaces, clear-desk arrangements and known hazards |
| Outstanding work | Condition observed, agreed initial tasks and separately quoted items |

Arrange codes and credential changes through your authorised workplace or building-management process. Do not circulate them in the procurement register or leave an old provider's access active by accident. Confirm completion with the responsible person.

## Agree the starting condition

Walk the site before commencement. Identify which concerns can be addressed by routine visits, which need an initial detail clean and which are maintenance or specialist issues. Record existing damage and surface-care instructions so neither party is guessing what happened before the first visit.

A useful starting record describes observable conditions: a marked glass panel, accumulated floor-edge dust or an area that cannot be accessed. It does not need claims about microbes, illness or an assumed previous provider's methods.

If periodic carpet care or internal glass is part of the proposal, confirm when that work is due. Starting a routine service does not mean every periodic task is completed on the first evening.

## First visit: check access before judging the whole service

Confirm the people attending have the agreed site instructions, can access the included areas and know the workplace contact. Agree how a failed-access event, a restricted room or an unexpected occupied area is reported.

After the visit, compare the result with the tasks due that day. Distinguish a missed included task from a task not yet scheduled or an item outside scope. Record the action and agree when it will be checked again. Avoid silently adding work to the regular visit.

## First-month review: close issues, then adjust

Set the review date with the provider rather than assuming a universal trial period or response deadline. Use a short register:

| Review field | Example of the information to record |
| --- | --- |
| Task due | The agreed room, surface and frequency |
| Observation | What was seen and when |
| Access | Whether the area was available |
| Action | Correction, clarification, maintenance referral or scope review |
| Owner and check date | Who follows up and when completion is reviewed |

Check that issues are closed, the site instructions remain accurate and consumables responsibilities are understood. If attendance changes, review the scope against use rather than simply carrying the original schedule forward.

For a worked quality-review method, see [what good commercial cleaning looks like](/blog/what-good-commercial-cleaning-looks-like). Our [four-page cleaning pack](/guides/workplace-cleaning-scope-checklist.pdf) includes an issue log and task schedule you can use with the provider.

## What the YOS service pathway looks like

YOS provides [commercial cleaning in Newcastle CBD and Lake Macquarie](/cleaning). Sarah oversees the cleaning relationship and quality assurance. We aim for consistent teams wherever possible, with documented scopes and site notes supporting handover when cover or a change is needed.

The starting point is a site inspection and a written proposal, not a promise to match an undefined existing price. Confirm the scope, service timing, access and commencement arrangements for your workplace before service begins.

## Changeover checklist

1. Record the specific service or scope issues you want resolved.
2. Review existing obligations and confirm the outgoing end date.
3. Inspect the site with the incoming provider and approve the written scope.
4. Agree initial, routine, periodic and excluded work separately.
5. Confirm access, induction, key custody and equipment responsibilities.
6. Record the starting condition without exposing confidential information.
7. Confirm the first visit and how access or service issues are reported.
8. Hold the agreed review and document any approved scope changes.

[Talk to YOS about a cleaning changeover](/cleaning#cleaning-quote-form). Share the address, intended timing and the main problem to resolve. Leave alarm codes and private records out of the enquiry.
